appraisal_events.evidence: « Odette le vit s’éloigner avec regret, elle n’osa pas ne pas revenir avec Swann, mais fut de mauvaise humeur en voiture »; to his question she answers « Bien entendu » « en haussant les épaules avec impatience ».
appraisal_events.explanation: Odette openly regrets Forcheville's departure and endures Swann only because she does not dare refuse him, so Swann is locally reduced to a tolerated companion whose company she answers with an impatient shrug. The narration presents her coldness as plain fact, not as Swann's suspicion.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Qu’est-ce que c’est exactement que cette Mme Verdurin ? un demi-castor ? dit Forcheville au peintre », immediately after Cottard's « J’ai rarement vu Mme Verdurin aussi en verve que ce soir ».
appraisal_events.explanation: Forcheville, as soon as he is out of the salon, questions the hostess's respectability to another guest, reducing her to a demeaning social category. The narrator reports the remark without comment, but its placement right after Cottard's admiring line exposes how little the clan's self-esteem is worth outside the house.

status_effects.explanation: Swann ends the evening clearly on the weak side of the relation: Odette leaves with him out of constraint, is in a bad humor, and dismisses his question with an impatient shrug.
Odette's regret at watching him go marks Forcheville as the man she would have preferred, so he gains locally at Swann's expense without doing anything himself.
Her standing is lowered by Forcheville's insinuating question about what she really is, which treats the mistress of the salon as a woman of doubtful position.

ambiguities: The opening speech (« Il est peut-être un peu péremptoire et un peu jovial pour mon goût... on sent qu’il sait tant de choses ») has no named target inside the passage: the man appraised is only the « il » of the preceding question, so this qualified praise is left unannotated rather than attached to a guessed referent.

The speaker of that reply is likewise unnamed; attributing it to Swann (the guest Mme Verdurin questions « sèchement », and the one still present at the end) is the strongest reading, but it is contextual, so no separate salon-disfavor event is recorded for him.
